note: The final syllable is reduced to a schwa in Britain but keeps a full /oʊ/ in America.

senses.definition: Complete and careful, with attention to every detail.
examples: The inspector gave the kitchen a thorough check.
She is thorough, so her reports rarely need corrections.
A thorough clean took most of the weekend.

senses.definition: A soft red fruit eaten raw or cooked, used widely as a vegetable in cooking.
examples: Slice the tomato thinly and season it with salt.
He grows six varieties of tomato in the greenhouse.
The sauce is simply tomato, garlic, and olive oil.

note: British English often palatalises the /tj/ to /tʃ/; American English drops the /j/ entirely.

senses.definition: The day of the week after Monday and before Wednesday.
examples: The class meets every Tuesday at six.
We fly out on Tuesday morning.
Last Tuesday was the wettest day of the year.

senses.definition: A natural substance found in food that the body needs in small amounts to stay healthy.
examples: Citrus fruit is a good source of vitamin C.
The doctor suggested a vitamin D supplement in winter.
A varied diet usually supplies every vitamin you need.

senses.definition: The clear liquid that falls as rain and that people and animals drink.
examples: Could I have a glass of water, please?
The water in the lake was surprisingly warm.
Turn the water off at the mains before you start.

senses.definition: To pour water on plants or land.
examples: Remember to water the tomatoes every evening.
The fields are watered by an old irrigation system.

senses.definition: The condition of the air and sky at a particular time and place: rain, sun, wind, and temperature.
examples: The weather turned during the night.
We will go ahead whatever the weather.
Cold weather is forecast for the rest of the week.

senses.definition: The earth and all the people, places, and things on it.
examples: She has travelled all over the world.
The news spread around the world in hours.

senses.definition: A particular area of activity or group of people.
examples: In the world of publishing, timing is everything.
He knows the academic world from the inside.

senses.definition: An African wild animal like a horse, with black and white stripes.
examples: A herd of zebra crossed the road ahead of us.
No two zebra have exactly the same pattern of stripes.
The zebra is closely related to the horse and the donkey.
